title: Defining the cellular microenvironment of sarcopenia in pancreatic cancer associated cachexia
summary:
Pancreatic cancer is a very aggressive disease with still very poor chances of survival. Many patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer suffer from cachexia during the course of the disease.
Cachexia leads to severe weight loss with a reduction in both fat mass and muscle mass, which is associated with a significant decline in quality of life.
The role of changes in muscle tissue in pancreatic cancer-associated cachexia has not yet been sufficiently researched. 
Therefore, the aim of this study is to characterize and understand in detail the changes in muscle tissue in pancreatic cancer-associated cachexia.

interventions.name: Control group: Living kidney donors - skeletal muscle tissue was collected intraoperatively
Pancreatic cancer patients without cachexia (defined by body weight development over the last six months) - skeletal muscle tissue was collected intraoperatively
Pancreatic cancer patients with cachexia (defined by body weight development over the last six months) - skeletal muscle tissue was collected intraoperatively

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent
Ability to give consent 
Pancreatic cancer 
Planned abdominal surgery 
Unintentional weight loss (yes and no)
Exclusion criteria:
Weight-modulating drugs (ozempic, mirtazapine, etc.) 
Weight-modulating surgeries
Chronic inflammatory diseases (IBS, rheumatic diseases, sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, COPD, etc.)
Other cancers
Revocation of written consent
